title: Lenin Wraps Theatrical Run at ₹69 Crore Worldwide, Marks Akhil Akkineni's First Career Hit
excerpt: The Telugu action drama fell just short of the ₹50 crore domestic net mark but emerged as a commercial success, crossing 200 million streaming minutes on ZEE5 within its first week.
body:
• Akhil Akkineni's Telugu action drama Lenin concluded its theatrical run with approximately ₹68.88 crore worldwide gross and ₹49 crore net in India.
  • The film emerged as Akkineni's first commercial hit in his 11-year career, though it narrowly missed the ₹50 crore domestic net milestone.
  • Lenin crossed 200 million streaming minutes on ZEE5 within its first week of digital release on August 7, signaling strong post-theatrical demand.
  • Produced on a budget of ₹50 crore, the film proved profitable for distributors despite slowing collections in its final weeks.

Akhil Akkineni's rural action drama Lenin has officially wrapped its theatrical run after completing one month in cinemas, closing at a worldwide gross of approximately ₹68.88 crore. The film, which released on July 10, 2026, earned around ₹49 crore net at the Indian box office — falling just short of the ₹50 crore mark that remained elusive through its final week of single-digit lakh daily collections.

A Career-Defining Moment for Akhil Akkineni

Despite missing the ₹50 crore net benchmark, Lenin represents a watershed moment for Akhil Akkineni. The film emerged as his first commercially successful venture in an 11-year career that had been marked by box office disappointments, most recently the 2023 debacle Agent. Trade analysts classified Lenin as a "Clean Hit," with distributors reporting profitable returns across key markets.

https://x.com/Koimoi/status/2088971920956100865

The bulk of Lenin's domestic business came from its home territory. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana contributed roughly ₹36.75 crore of the total gross — with Nizam accounting for ₹16.50 crore, Andhra Pradesh ₹16 crore, and the Ceded region around ₹4.25 crore. Karnataka added approximately ₹4 crore, while the rest of India contributed about ₹1 crore.

"Lenin is a rooted, intense rural drama. For those willing to sit with a slow-building story about friendship, loyalty, and love turning into conflict, it largely delivers, anchored by a career-best performance from Akhil Akkineni."

— Yashaswini Sri, The Indian Express

Box Office Trajectory

Lenin opened strongly with ₹7.50 crore on its first day and built momentum through a ₹27.50 crore opening weekend. The first week closed at ₹41.75 crore gross (₹36.65 crore net), establishing a solid base. The second week added ₹10.17 crore net, while the third week brought in ₹2.06 crore as collections tapered. By Day 23, daily earnings had dropped to ₹8 lakh, with the film's theatrical window effectively exhausted.

Produced on a reported budget of ₹50 crore by Nagarjuna Akkineni, Yuriy Krestinskiy, Suryadevara Naga Vamsi, and Elena Yatsura under the Annapurna Studios banner, the film's worldwide gross crossed its production cost, making it a commercially viable project. Shloka Entertainments handled U.S. distribution, while Naga Vamsi independently managed the Andhra Pradesh release.

Digital Afterlife on ZEE5

Lenin's post-theatrical performance has been equally noteworthy. The film debuted on ZEE5 on August 7 and crossed 200 million streaming minutes within its first week — a significant digital milestone for a mid-budget Telugu film. However, the OTT release came with an unexpected limitation: despite initial announcements of multi-language availability, only the Telugu version was made available for streaming at launch.

Director Murali Kishor Abburu and producer Naga Vamsi visited the Tirumala temple on August 11 to offer prayers following the film's successful theatrical and digital run — a traditional gesture in the Telugu film industry marking a project's completion.

Mixed Critical Reception

Critics offered a divided assessment. The Hindu's Sangeetha Devi Dundoo acknowledged Akhil's growth as an actor but noted the film relied too heavily on "the mass-action template." India Today praised director Abburu's ambition but said the film suffered from "missed opportunities." The Hollywood Reporter India called it a "shopworn revenge drama" while praising the lead performances and the film's Mahabharata parallels. On audience platforms, Lenin maintained an 8.9 rating on BookMyShow with over 53,000 votes.

What It Means for Tollywood

At the film's success meet, veteran actor Nagarjuna — Akhil's father and one of the film's producers — used the occasion to urge the Telugu film industry to end its pattern of last-minute release delays. "We must finish films well in advance," Nagarjuna said, recalling an earlier era when productions were completed weeks before their scheduled release. Lenin itself had been postponed from its original May 1 date to June 26 to avoid clashing with Ram Charan's Peddi, before being pushed again to July 10 for post-production work.

For Akhil Akkineni, the film's commercial performance — combined with strong streaming numbers — provides a foundation to build on. For Tollywood, Lenin's trajectory offers a familiar lesson: a well-executed mid-budget film with strong regional appeal can still deliver solid returns, even in an era of blockbuster-or-bust economics.
